ideas.risks: May only confirm an abstract tautological value identity; no tail or rate content. The proof depends sensitively on the chosen policy class and on ex-ante randomization making C convex.
ideas.summary: Write the finite-grid arbitrary-class ba dual as a standalone theorem: define the common randomized policy class, C subset l-infinity(Theta), norm closure, separation from C-X_+, positivity of the separator, normalization to ba_1^+, and the reverse weak-duality inequality. Track whether the theorem gives value equality only or also approximate policies.
ideas.title: Referee-Proof ba Dual
ideas.why_promising: The iteration 20 solver leans on this dual but does not prove it. A clean proof would secure the strongest exact arbitrary-class value statement and clarify exactly what remains unsolved.

ideas.risks: Could become theorem hygiene rather than new insight, and standard measurable-version facts may have hidden null-set pitfalls. It still will not handle continuum quotes or action-dependent prices.
ideas.summary: Complete the payoff-measure dominated no-gap theorem for the original Borel policy model, not just completed L-infinity kernels. Prove both inclusions C_Borel subset C_Linfty and C_Linfty subset C_Borel under the common Borel seed/state model, using Borel versions, finite-action randomization, and domination of payoff-weighted measures.
ideas.title: Borel Policy No-Gap Bridge
ideas.why_promising: This would turn the most useful interpretable infinite-class theorem from a conditional completed-kernel result into a usable result for ordinary policies.

ideas.risks: Prior attempts show severe collapse modes: shared types reveal too quickly, independent bits wash out against one fixed comparator, and persistent quotes can violate tail envelopes. The construction may prove an impossibility heuristic instead of a lower bound.
ideas.summary: Investigate limited-leakage or noisy common-parameter lower bounds for power-tail classes. Build a finite-grid family where each delayed tail event has probability q and revenue separation gamma but terminal observations have controlled KL/TV; compute the finite-grid Bayes value and check whether kappa >= gamma^2/q blocks rate matching.
ideas.title: Limited-Leakage Tail Lower Bounds
ideas.why_promising: Matching the truncation upper rate is the main unresolved rate question. The existing qD atom is too weak, so a Fano/Le Cam construction is the most concrete next path.

ideas.risks: The desired comparator-specific delay theorem may be false. Even if true in two arms, extension to many dyadic (H,b) arms may fail or pay hidden max-delay costs.
ideas.summary: Focus on the two-arm delayed-advantage game. Starting from the solvency invariant A_T >= -B, test reserve or fractional-wealth rules that can recover after negative delayed feedback and prove or refute simultaneous bounds A_T >= -O(sqrt T) and A_T >= S_T-O(sqrt(TD)).
ideas.title: Comparator-Specific Delay Experts
ideas.why_promising: A proof would give a tail-adaptive upper bound min_H {delta_T(H)+sqrt(TH log K)}. A counterexample would sharply delimit what adaptive truncation can achieve.

ideas.risks: May only repackage known value-tail quantities and still cannot overcome the hidden/labeled no-go without adding public-prefix information. There is a danger of accidentally stating another scalar-tail false theorem.
ideas.summary: Develop the last-exceedance identity into a predictability-aware condition. Express V_T, delta_T(H), and Bayes gaps using L_a=max{s<=T:P_s>a} and payoff-weighted public-prefix measures, then test whether a last-exceedance truncation modulus plus an observability term yields a checkable sufficient/necessary pair.
ideas.title: Predictable Last-Exceedance Tails
ideas.why_promising: First-hitting beta is the wrong raw object. Last-exceedance calculus directly describes fixed-comparator value and may expose a more natural structural condition than the ba support function.

ideas.risks: Identifiable classes may be easy for trivial decoding reasons, while nonidentifiable Borel gaps may be hard or pathological. Weak/Feller continuity alone is already known insufficient.
ideas.summary: Search for natural infinite-class no-gap conditions beyond payoff-measure domination: identifiable Borel parameter classes with measurable decoders, dominated approximations with explicit value-error constants, or compact statistical experiments. In parallel, try to construct a Borel, nondominated, nonidentifiable class with a genuine finite-subclass/full-class gap.
ideas.title: Natural Infinite-Class No-Gap Conditions
ideas.why_promising: The finite-prior Bayes formula is interpretable, but arbitrary infinite classes currently need ba priors. Better no-gap hypotheses could make the characterization useful without finitely additive objects.

ideas.risks: This addresses a neighboring regime rather than the original horizon-aware minimax problem. The lower bound must avoid being defeated by doubling or by horizon-dependent randomization.
ideas.summary: Formalize the anytime known-law obstruction suggested by super-growing two-deadline deterministic blocks. Prove or refute that one horizon-free policy for a known infinite exogenous sequence must have linear regret on some horizon even though every finite horizon has an O(1) law-aware oracle.
ideas.title: Anytime Known-Law Boundary
ideas.why_promising: It would sharpen the model taxonomy and explain exactly why the known-law oracle is horizon-aware. This prevents false fixed-process necessity claims from reappearing.

ideas.risks: May be mostly expository, and the result will still be a no-go rather than a positive characterization. Need avoid overclaiming beyond per-world scalar profiles.
ideas.summary: Package the hidden/labeled q-scaled terminal pair as a formal impossibility theorem for scalar per-world tail profiles. Define a broad class of profile-based criteria, prove hidden and labeled classes have identical legal per-world reward/delay/truncation data, and quantify the qD/8 versus zero regret separation.
ideas.title: Scalar-Tail Impossibility Theorem
ideas.why_promising: This would give a crisp negative answer to the original beta-style characterization goal and justify shifting effort toward public-prefix predictability or reward-set conditions.
